feed.title: AMD, Cisco and HUMAIN Expand Saudi Arabia’s AI Infrastructure as AMD Instinct Systems Go Live
feed.summary: AMD, Cisco, and HUMAIN have announced that AMD Instinct MI355X GPU-based AI infrastructure, utilizing Cisco Silicon One-based AI networking, is now operational in Saudi Arabia, serving HUMAIN customers. This marks a significant step towards building an open, large-scale AI platform in the region. The companies plan to expand this infrastructure to 250 MW, powered by AMD Instinct MI400 Series GPUs and AMD ROCm open software, starting in 2027, with a long-term goal of deploying up to 1 GW of AI infrastructure by 2030 to meet growing demand.

feed.title: Broadcom’s VMware Private AI Cloud spans infrastructure, agents, data and security
feed.summary: Broadcom has launched VMware Private AI Cloud, an integrated software stack designed for enterprises to build and run AI applications alongside traditional workloads, ensuring data, model, and infrastructure control. Broadcom also introduced TrueSource, a portfolio of commercially supported open-source software, emphasizing secure software supply chains and enterprise-grade AI deployment.

feed.title: Ottawa pumps $195 million into quantum manufacturing by Xanadu
feed.summary: The Canadian federal government is investing $195 million into Toronto-based Xanadu Quantum Technologies Inc. to establish an advanced manufacturing facility. feed.title: The network becomes the computer as Cisco and Nvidia accelerate AI factory rack-scale
feed.summary: Cisco and Nvidia are partnering to advance AI factory infrastructure, shifting the focus from GPU acquisition to AI production and defining the architecture for AI factories. The initiative focuses on optimizing the entire AI infrastructure lifecycle, from deployment to continuous operation, by treating the AI factory as a single distributed computer.

feed.title: Data pipeline woes push AMD, Supermicro, MinIO to lakehouse
feed.summary: Despite rapid advances in AI, enterprises still face significant data pipeline challenges, with over 80% of data being unstructured and largely inaccessible to AI systems. This partnership aims to provide pre-validated, flexible solutions that balance hardware and software components for optimal performance in AI workloads.
